name: India EO Query Benchmark v1
description: Natural-language questions about Indian Earth observation, with the routing each one should produce. Existing agent benchmarks (GeoLLM-Engine, GeoAgentBench) are not India-specific and do not cover Indian cropping seasons, district naming, or monsoon phrasing.

revisions.note: Three labels corrected after the first model run. Vembanad lake is in Kerala, and Kutch and Gurgaon are real districts, so 'no region' was factually wrong in each case - the model was right and the benchmark was not. Corrected because the labels were incorrect, not because the model disagreed with them.

One further label corrected: 'How much has Bangalore grown since 2019' names Bangalore, which is a resolvable district, so expecting no region was wrong for the same reason as the three above. No label has been changed merely because the model disagreed with it - each correction is a factual error in the original labelling.

Added region_resolvable, splitting a field that was conflating two different jobs. The original schema scored extraction and resolution together, so a correct extraction of an unresolvable place ('marathwada') counted as a failure. That is a benchmark design error, not a system error: the router reads the question, the resolver owns the gazetteer. Marathwada, Vidarbha and Bundelkhand are now labelled as correctly extracted and correctly unresolvable. This is a schema change rather than another relabelling - the three cases still test that informal regions are handled, but they now test the right thing.

fields.question: what a user would type
fields.analysis_type: expected analysis, or null when the question is out of scope
fields.region: the place name that should be EXTRACTED from the question, lowercase, or null when no place is named
fields.region_resolvable: whether that name exists in FAO GAUL 2015 and will resolve to a geometry. Absent means true.
fields.comparison: true when the question asks for change rather than a snapshot
fields.period_contains: a date the chosen window must include, or null

scoring_note: Extraction and resolution are separate jobs and are scored separately. The router's task is to report what the question said; deciding whether that place exists belongs to the region resolver, which has the gazetteer. Returning 'marathwada' for a question about Marathwada is CORRECT extraction, even though Marathwada is a cultural region spanning eight districts and will not resolve. Returning null there would assert that no place was named, which is false and produces a worse error message for the user.
